summary:
The Things We Left Behind is an interactive exploration game set on Mars. Players guide a small rover through different regions, discover the stories of past spacecraft, complete activities based on their missions, and unlock an archive of images and information. The game works in a web browser: players move, interact with objects and characters, and make choices using a keyboard, mouse, or touch controls.
The project combines storytelling with learning. Its main benefit is that it makes the history of Mars exploration more engaging than a list of facts. We want players to understand what earlier missions discovered and to feel how each one contributed to the missions that followed.
We built the game with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, using an HTML canvas for the visuals and gameplay. It runs on a computer or mobile device without requiring special hardware or an installation. Images, sound, and saved progress add to the experience.
My creative approach was to turn real mission history into places to explore, conversations to follow, and activities to complete. we designed the visuals around a retro space-monitor style. While developing it, we considered readability, mobile controls, image loading, and how to keep activity accessible across devices.
details:
The Things We Left Behind is an educational Mars exploration game built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Players control a rover across six regions, interact with characters based on spacecraft missions, complete fourteen activities, and unlock an archive of mission images and stories. Its narrative introduces the hardware, explains its purpose, and presents discoveries that contributed to planetary science.

The game renders its world, sprites, dialogue, interface, and activities on a 960 × 540 HTML canvas. A JavaScript animation loop updates movement, collision detection, animation, game states, and interaction logic. CSS scales the canvas for different viewports. Keyboard and mouse input support desktop play; pointer events and on-screen controls provide touch input on mobile devices.

Browser local storage saves player progress, discoveries, and settings between sessions. A custom asset loader reads an image manifest and falls back to probing image files when the manifest is missing or outdated. Asset URLs resolve relative to the game scripts, supporting local folders and hosted project subpaths. Web Audio provides music and sound effects.

Our development process combined mission research, narrative design, pixel-art presentation, and cross-device testing. We structured educational content as explorable environments, dialogue, interactive challenges, and archive entries to help school-age learners and casual space enthusiasts connect spacecraft hardware with its scientific purpose and results.
